newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RELIEVED BROWN WARNS SWEDEN AND AUSTRIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RELIEVED BROWN WARNS SWEDEN AND AUSTRIA.

text.p: Scotland coach Craig Brown delivered a World Cup warning to rivals Sweden and Austria after his side overcame a stubborn Estonia 2-0 in their vital group four qualifier on Saturday.
Brown breathed a sigh of relief when the Scots wrapped up all three points thanks to Tom Boyd's first goal for his country in his 43rd international and an own goal from Janek Meet.

The result helped ease the embarrassing memory of the 0-0 draw with the Estonians last month in Monaco, the match re-arranged after Estonia failed to show up when the tie was originally due to be played last October.

It leaves Scotland four points ahead of Austria at the top of the standings with Austria visiting Glasgow on Wednesday. Scotland have 11 points, Austria seven from two games fewer. Sweden are third on six.
"Estonia will damage others in this group," said Brown. "I am convinced they will take points from our rivals and it would surprise me if the Swedes or the Austrians take full points from them.
"They were hard to break down and we might have lost a goal ourselves if it had not been for the outstanding display of our goalkeeper Jim Leighton."
The Scots made the vital breakthrough when Celtic defender Boyd scored after 25 minutes, heading home a parried save from Estonia's Mart Poom, who has just joined Derby County in England.

It was his first goal in his 43rd match for Scotland and he joked afterwards: "I don't really know how to celebrate goals. Still, it gives us a good advantage at the top of the group but that that is only an advantage if we can beat the Austrians next week.
"But this was some consolation after letting ourselves down in Monaco and we are now back on course for the finals."

Poom said: "Scotland are a big footballing country and deserve to be at the World Cup finals. Hopefully we can now do them a favour by taking points off other teams and we are confident we can do that."
Scotland's victory was sealed in the 53rd minute when Boyd crossed and the ball went in off Meet.
Although the capacity crowd totalled only 18,000, the match was played out in a passionate, carnival atmosphere at Rugby Park, staging its first international since 1910.

A crowd of 55,000 is expected at Celtic Park for Wednesday's match and the Scottish Football Association are planning to open their offices on Monday, a public holiday, to cope with the expected rush for tickets.
